newsitem.title: ARGENTINA: Argentine bonds end narrowly mixed.
newsitem.headline: Argentine bonds end narrowly mixed.

text.p: Argentine bonds closed narrowly mixed Wednesday in quiet trading and were seen unchanged ahead of Thursday's auction of five-year Bonte Treasury bonds, dealers said.

"Prices steadied a bit as the U.S. long bond yield slipped today, but overall the market was sluggish," one trader said. "We continue to like Argentine bonds at these prices, but we think there may be some more selling."
The country's FRB Brady bond due 2005 firmed 1/8 to 94-1/4 while the dollar-denominated Bocon Previsional 2 was down $0.1 at 121.
The benchmark 30-year U.S. Treasury bond closed at 6.69 percent against 6.72 percent Tuesday.
"The Beige Book helped U.S. Treasuries today, showing labor markets are tight but there still is really no wage pressure," another dealer said.
Traders forecast Argentina's $750 million Bonte auction Thursday would fetch interest of between 8.75 percent and 9.0 percent.
